title.zh: 卷六十四 後蜀世家第四: 孟知祥
title.en: Volume 64: Hereditary House of Later Shu
title.raw: 卷六十四 後蜀世家第四: 孟知祥 Volume 64: Hereditary House of Later Shu

sentences.zh: 孟知祥，字保胤，邢州龍岡人也。

translations.literal: Meng Zhixiang, style name Baoyin, was a man of Longgang in Xing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Zhixiang, whose courtesy name was Baoyin, was a native of Longgang in Xing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 其叔父遷，當唐之末，據邢、洺、磁三州，為晉所虜。

translations.literal: His uncle Qian, at the end of the Tang, held the three prefectures of Xing, Ming, and Ci, and was captured by Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Qian, in the closing years of the Tang, seized control of Xing, Ming, and Ci prefectures and was taken captive by Jin.

sentences.zh: 晉王以遷守澤潞，梁兵攻晉，遷以澤潞降梁。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin had Qian defend Ze and Lu; Liang troops attacked Jin, and Qian surrendered Ze and Lu to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin put Qian in charge of Ze and Lu; when Liang forces attacked Jin, Qian surrendered those circuits to Liang.

sentences.zh: 知祥父道，獨留事晉而不顯。

translations.literal: Zhixiang's father Dao alone remained to serve Jin and did not become prominent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixiang's father Dao alone stayed on to serve Jin and never rose to prominence.

sentences.zh: 及知祥壯，晉王以其弟克讓女妻之，以為左教練使。

translations.literal: When Zhixiang came of age, the Prince of Jin gave him in marriage a daughter of his younger brother Kerang and appointed him Left Training Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhixiang reached manhood, the Prince of Jin married him to a daughter of his younger brother Kerang and made him Left Training Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 莊宗為晉王，以知祥為中門使。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong was Prince of Jin, he made Zhixiang Commissioner of the Inner Gate.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhuangzong was still Prince of Jin, he appointed Zhixiang Commissioner of the Inner Gate.

sentences.zh: 前此為中門使者多以罪誅，知祥懼，求他職，莊宗命知祥薦可代己者，知祥因薦郭崇韜自代，崇韜德之，知祥遷馬步軍都虞候。

translations.literal: Previously those who served as Commissioner of the Inner Gate were mostly executed for crimes; Zhixiang was afraid and sought another post. Zhuangzong ordered Zhixiang to recommend someone who could replace him; Zhixiang therefore recommended Guo Chongtao to replace himself. Chongtao was grateful to him, and Zhixiang was transferred to Chief Garrison Officer of the horse and foot armies.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier holders of the Inner Gate commission had mostly been put to death on criminal charges, and Zhixiang, fearing the same fate, asked for another post. Zhuangzong told him to name his own successor; Zhixiang recommended Guo Chongtao to take his place. Chongtao was grateful, and Zhixiang was promoted to Chief Garrison Officer of the horse and foot armies.

sentences.zh: 莊宗建號，以太原為北京，以知祥為太原尹、北京留守。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong established his reign title, he made Taiyuan the Northern Capital and appointed Zhixiang Taiyuan Intendant and Northern Capital regent.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhuangzong proclaimed his dynasty, he designated Taiyuan the Northern Capital and appointed Zhixiang Taiyuan Intendant and regent of the Northern Capital.

sentences.zh: 魏王繼岌代蜀，郭崇韜為招討使，崇韜臨訣，白曰：「即臣等平蜀，陛下擇帥以守西川，無如孟知祥者。

translations.literal: Prince of Wei Jiji campaigned against Shu; Guo Chongtao was Pacification Commissioner. At parting Chongtao reported, saying: "Once your servants pacify Shu, Your Majesty should choose a commander to guard the western circuit—none is like Meng Zhixiang.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Wei Jiji marched against Shu, Guo Chongtao served as Pacification Commissioner. On taking leave he said to the throne: "Once we pacify Shu, Your Majesty should choose a governor to hold the western circuit—and none is better suited than Meng Zhixiang.

sentences.zh: 」已而唐兵破蜀，莊宗遂以知祥為成都尹、劍南西川節度副大使。

translations.literal: " Before long Tang troops defeated Shu, and Zhuangzong then appointed Zhixiang Chengdu Intendant and Vice Commissioner of the Sword-South Western Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: " Before long Tang forces overran Shu, and Zhuangzong appointed Zhixiang Chengdu Intendant and deputy military commissioner of the Sword-South Western Circuit.

sentences.zh: 知祥馳至京師，莊宗戒有司盛供帳，多出內府珍奇諸物以宴勞之。

translations.literal: Zhixiang hurried to the capital; Zhuangzong ordered the officials to prepare lavish supplies and brought out many rare objects from the inner palace to feast and reward him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixiang rode posthaste to the capital, where Zhuangzong ordered officials to lay on a lavish reception and drew many rare treasures from the inner palace stores to feast and honor him.

sentences.zh: 酒酣，語及平昔，以為笑樂，嘆曰：「繼岌前日乳臭兒爾，乃能為吾平定兩川，吾徒老矣，孺子可喜，然益令人悲爾！

translations.literal: When the wine had gone deep, they spoke of former days as matter for laughter and pleasure. He sighed and said: "Jiji was only a milk-smelling boy the other day, yet he could pacify the two circuits for me. We alone have grown old; the lad is a delight—yet it makes one all the sadder!
translations.idiomatic: As the drinking deepened they reminisced about old times with laughter and pleasure. Zhuangzong sighed and said: "Jiji was only a milk-faced boy the other day, yet he could pacify both river circuits for me. We have grown old; the lad is heartening—and yet all the more heartbreaking!

sentences.zh: 吾憶先帝棄世時，疆土侵削，僅保一隅，豈知今日奄有天下，九州四海，珍奇異產，充刃吾府！

translations.literal: I recall when the former emperor left the world, the realm was encroached upon and cut down, and we barely preserved one corner—who could know that today we suddenly possess all under Heaven, the nine provinces and four seas, with rare and strange products filling my palace!
translations.idiomatic: I remember when the former emperor died: our territory was being whittled away and we barely held a single corner. Who could have imagined that today we would suddenly possess the empire—the nine provinces and four seas—with rare and wondrous goods cramming my palace!

sentences.zh: 」因指以示知祥，曰：「吾聞蜀土之富，無異於此，以卿親賢，故以相付。」

translations.literal: " He then pointed to show Zhixiang and said: "I have heard that the wealth of Shu is no different from this; because you are close and worthy, I therefore entrust it to you."
translations.idiomatic: " He gestured at the display and told Zhixiang: "I am told the wealth of Shu is no different from this. Because you are both kin and worthy, I entrust it to you."

sentences.zh: 同光四年正月戊辰，知祥至成都，而崇韜已死。

translations.literal: On the wuchen day of the first month of the fourth year of Tongguang, Zhixiang reached Chengdu, but Chongtao was already dead.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuchen day of the first month in the fourth year of Tongguang, Zhixiang reached Chengdu—only to learn that Chongtao was already dead.

sentences.zh: 魏王繼岌引軍東歸，先鋒康延孝反，攻破漢州。

translations.literal: Prince of Wei Jiji led the army east in withdrawal; the vanguard Kang Yanxiao rebelled and stormed Han Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Wei Jiji withdrew eastward with his army; the vanguard commander Kang Yanxiao mutinied and seized Han Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 知祥遣大將李仁罕會任圜、董璋等兵擊破延孝，知祥得其將李肇、侯弘實及其兵數千以歸。

translations.literal: Zhixiang sent the great general Li Renhan to join the troops of Ren Yuan, Dong Zhang, and others to defeat Yanxiao; Zhixiang obtained his generals Li Zhao, Hou Hongshi, and several thousand of their soldiers and brought them back.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixiang sent his chief general Li Renhan to join Ren Yuan, Dong Zhang, and others in crushing Yanxiao; he took Yanxiao's generals Li Zhao and Hou Hongshi, along with several thousand troops, back into his own service.

sentences.zh: 而莊宗崩，魏王繼岌死，明宗入立。

translations.literal: Then Zhuangzong died; Prince of Wei Jiji died; Mingzong entered and took the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong then died, Prince of Wei Jiji died as well, and Mingzong ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 知祥乃訓練兵甲，陰有王蜀之志。

translations.literal: Zhixiang then trained weapons and armor and secretly harbored the ambition to become king of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixiang thereupon drilled his arms and armor and secretly nurtured the ambition to rule Shu as king.

sentences.zh: 益置義勝、定遠、驍銳、義寧、飛棹等軍七萬餘人，命李仁罕、趙廷隱、張業等分將之。

translations.literal: He further established the armies of Righteous Victory, Settled Distance, Fierce Sharpness, Righteous Tranquility, Flying Oar, and others—more than seventy thousand men—and ordered Li Renhan, Zhao Tingyin, Zhang Ye, and others to command them in divisions.
translations.idiomatic: He further raised more than seventy thousand men in the armies of Righteous Victory, Settled Distance, Fierce Sharpness, Righteous Tranquility, Flying Oar, and the like, placing Li Renhan, Zhao Tingyin, Zhang Ye, and others in divided command.

sentences.zh: 初，魏王之班師也，知祥率成都富人及王氏故臣家，得錢六百萬緡以犒軍，其餘者猶二百萬。

translations.literal: At first, when the Prince of Wei withdrew his army, Zhixiang led the wealthy of Chengdu and the households of former ministers of the Wang clan to obtain six million strings of cash to reward the army; what remained was still two million.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Wei first withdrew his army, Zhixiang levied six million strings of cash from Chengdu's wealthy and from families of former Wang ministers to reward the troops; two million strings still remained.

sentences.zh: 任圜自蜀入為相，兼判三司，素知蜀所余錢。

translations.literal: Ren Yuan came from Shu to serve as chief minister and concurrently oversaw the Three Bureaus; he had long known of the money remaining in Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Yuan came up from Shu to serve as chief minister and concurrently head of the Three Bureaus, and he had long known about the surplus funds in Shu.

sentences.zh: 是冬，知祥拜侍中，乃以太僕卿趙季良賫官告賜之，因以為三川制置使，督蜀犒軍余錢送京師，且制置兩川征賦。

translations.literal: That winter Zhixiang was invested as Palace Attendant; the Court then sent Grand Master of the Stud Zhao Jiliang bearing the official patent to confer it, and at the same time made him Commissioner for the Three Rivers to supervise sending the remaining Shu reward money to the capital and to regulate the taxes and levies of the two circuits.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Zhixiang received appointment as Palace Attendant. The court sent Grand Master of the Stud Zhao Jiliang with the patent of office and, at the same time, named him Commissioner for the Three Rivers to oversee shipment of the remaining Shu reward funds to the capital and to regulate taxation in both circuits.

sentences.zh: 知祥怒，不奉詔。

translations.literal: Zhixiang was angry and did not obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixiang was furious and refused to comply.

sentences.zh: 然知祥與季良有舊，遂留之。

translations.literal: Yet Zhixiang and Jiliang had old ties, so he kept him.
translations.idiomatic: But Zhixiang and Jiliang were old acquaintances, so he kept him at his side.

sentences.zh: 樞密使安重誨頗疑知祥有異志，思有以制之。

translations.literal: Chief Palace Secretary An Chonghui greatly suspected that Zhixiang had a different intent and thought of means to control him.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Palace Secretary An Chonghui strongly suspected Zhixiang of disloyal intent and looked for ways to restrain him.

sentences.zh: 初，知祥鎮蜀，莊宗以宦者焦彥賓為監軍，明宗入立，悉誅宦者，罷諸道監軍。

translations.literal: At first, when Zhixiang governed Shu, Zhuangzong had the eunuch Jiao Yanbin as army supervisor; when Mingzong took the throne he executed all eunuchs and abolished army supervisors in every circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhixiang first took command in Shu, Zhuangzong had appointed the eunuch Jiao Yanbin army supervisor. After Mingzong's accession he executed the eunuchs and abolished army supervisors in every circuit.

sentences.zh: 彥賓已罷，重誨復以客省使李嚴為監軍。

translations.literal: Yanbin had already been dismissed, but Chonghui again appointed Guest Reception Commissioner Li Yan as army supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbin had already been removed, yet Chonghui appointed Guest Reception Commissioner Li Yan as army supervisor once more.

sentences.zh: 嚴前使蜀，既歸而獻策伐蜀，蜀人皆惡之，而知祥亦怒曰：「焦彥賓以例罷，而諸道皆廢監軍，獨吾軍置之，是嚴欲以蜀再為功也。

translations.literal: Yan had previously been sent to Shu; after returning he presented a plan to attack Shu, and all the people of Shu hated him. Zhixiang also angrily said: "Jiao Yanbin was dismissed according to precedent and every circuit abolished its army supervisor—yet alone in my army one is placed. This means Yan wishes to make Shu his achievement again.
translations.idiomatic: Yan had earlier been sent to Shu and, on returning, proposed a plan to conquer it, so the people of Shu detested him. Zhixiang too said in anger: "Jiao Yanbin was dismissed by precedent and every circuit abolished its supervisor—yet mine alone gets one. Yan means to win fresh glory by attacking Shu again.

sentences.zh: 」掌書記母昭裔及諸將吏皆請止嚴而無內，知祥曰：「吾將有以待其來！

translations.literal: " Recorder Mu Zhaoyi and the various generals and officials all asked to stop Yan and not let him enter. Zhixiang said: "I shall have means to await his coming!
translations.idiomatic: " Recorder Mu Zhaoyi and the other officers all urged that Yan be stopped at the border. Zhixiang said: "I have my own way of dealing with him when he arrives!

sentences.zh: 」嚴至境上，遣人持書候知祥，知祥盛兵見之，冀嚴懼而不來，嚴聞之自若。

translations.literal: " When Yan reached the border, he sent a man bearing a letter to greet Zhixiang. Zhixiang displayed his forces in strength to receive him, hoping Yan would be afraid and not come; when Yan heard of it he remained composed.
translations.idiomatic: " When Yan reached the frontier he sent ahead a letter of greeting. Zhixiang paraded his troops in force, hoping Yan would be frightened off—but Yan, hearing of it, remained unmoved.

sentences.zh: 天成二年正月，嚴至成都，知祥置酒召嚴。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Tiancheng, Yan reached Chengdu; Zhixiang set out wine and summoned Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year of Tiancheng, Yan arrived in Chengdu, and Zhixiang held a banquet and summoned him.

sentences.zh: 是時，焦彥賓雖罷，猶在蜀，嚴於懷中出詔示知祥以誅彥賓，知祥不聽，因責嚴曰：「今諸方鎮已罷監軍，公何得來此？

translations.literal: At that time, although Jiao Yanbin had been dismissed, he was still in Shu. Yan took an edict from his bosom to show Zhixiang for executing Yanbin; Zhixiang would not listen and therefore reproached Yan, saying: "Now every defense command has abolished its army supervisor—how dare you come here?
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Yanbin, though dismissed, was still in Shu. Yan produced from his robe an edict ordering Yanbin's execution. Zhixiang refused to comply and rebuked him: "Every defense command has abolished its supervisor—what right have you to come here?

sentences.zh: 」目客將王彥銖執嚴下，斬之。

translations.literal: " He signaled the guest officer Wang Yanzhen to seize Yan, take him down, and behead him.
translations.idiomatic: " He signaled his guest officer Wang Yanzhen to seize Yan, drag him down, and behead him.

sentences.zh: 明宗不能詰。

translations.literal: Mingzong could not hold him to account.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong could not call him to account.

sentences.zh: 初，知祥鎮蜀，遣人迎其家屬於太原，行至鳳翔，鳳翔節度使李從嚴聞知祥殺李嚴，以為知祥反矣，遂留之。

translations.literal: At first, when Zhixiang governed Shu, he sent men to bring his family from Taiyuan; when they reached Fengxiang, Fengxiang military commissioner Li Congyan heard that Zhixiang had killed Li Yan and thought Zhixiang had rebelled, so he detained them.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhixiang first took command in Shu he had sent for his family in Taiyuan. At Fengxiang, military commissioner Li Congyan, hearing that Zhixiang had killed Li Yan, assumed he had rebelled and detained them.

sentences.zh: 明宗既不能詰，而欲以恩信懷之，乃遣客省使李仁矩慰諭知祥，並送瓊華公主及其子昶等歸之。

translations.literal: Mingzong, unable to hold him to account yet wishing to win him with kindness and trust, then sent Guest Reception Commissioner Li Renju to console and instruct Zhixiang, and also sent back Princess Qionghua and his son Chang and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to punish him yet wishing to win him with kindness, Mingzong sent Guest Reception Commissioner Li Renju to reassure Zhixiang and returned Princess Qionghua, his son Chang, and the rest of his household.

sentences.zh: 知祥因請趙季良為節度副使，事無大小，皆與參決。

translations.literal: Zhixiang thereupon requested Zhao Jiliang as deputy military commissioner; matters great and small were all decided with his participation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixiang then asked that Zhao Jiliang be made deputy military commissioner and consulted him on every matter, large or small.

sentences.zh: 三年，唐徙季良為果州團練使，以何瓚為節度副使。

translations.literal: In the third year Tang transferred Jiliang to be regimental commissioner of Guo Prefecture and appointed He Zan as deputy military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the Tang court transferred Jiliang to regimental commissioner of Guo Prefecture and appointed He Zan deputy military commissioner in his place.

sentences.zh: 知祥得制書匿之，表留季良，不許。

translations.literal: Zhixiang obtained the commission document and concealed it; he memorialized to retain Jiliang, but it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixiang received the commission, hid it, and memorialized to keep Jiliang; the court refused.

sentences.zh: 乃遣其將雷廷魯至京師論請，明宗不得已而從之。

translations.literal: He then sent his general Lei Tinglu to the capital to argue the request; Mingzong had no choice but to accede.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent his general Lei Tinglu to the capital to press the request, and Mingzong reluctantly agreed.

sentences.zh: 是時，瓚行至綿谷，懼不敢進，知祥乃奏瓚為行軍司馬。

translations.literal: At that time Zan had reached Miangu but was afraid and did not dare advance; Zhixiang then memorialized to make Zan campaigning marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He Zan had reached Miangu but dared not go farther; Zhixiang thereupon memorialized to appoint him campaigning marshal.

sentences.zh: 是歲，唐師伐荊南，詔知祥以兵下峽，知祥遣毛重威率兵三千戍夔州。

translations.literal: That year Tang troops attacked Southern Jing; the edict ordered Zhixiang to lead troops down the gorges. Zhixiang sent Mao Chongwei to lead three thousand troops to garrison Kui Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: That year, as Tang forces campaigned against Southern Jing, the court ordered Zhixiang to send troops through the gorges. He dispatched Mao Chongwei with three thousand men to garrison Kui Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 已而荊南高季興死，其子從誨請命，知祥請罷戍兵，不許。

translations.literal: Before long Gao Jixing of Southern Jing died; his son Conghui requested investiture. Zhixiang asked to withdraw the garrison troops; it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Gao Jixing of Southern Jing died and his son Conghui submitted to the throne. Zhixiang asked to withdraw the garrison, but the court refused.

sentences.zh: 知祥諷重威以兵鼓噪，潰而歸，唐以詔書劾重威，知祥奏請無劾，由是唐大臣益以知祥為必反。

translations.literal: Zhixiang hinted to Chongwei that the troops should raise a clamor, break, and return. Tang impeached Chongwei by edict; Zhixiang memorialized asking that he not be impeached. From this Tang ministers increasingly regarded Zhixiang as certain to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixiang prompted Chongwei to let his men raise a clamor and break ranks for home. The Tang court impeached Chongwei by edict, but Zhixiang memorialized against the charge. Tang ministers now increasingly assumed Zhixiang would surely rebel.

sentences.zh: 四年，明宗將有事於南郊，遣李仁矩責知祥助禮錢一百萬緡。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Mingzong was about to perform the southern suburban sacrifice and sent Li Renju to demand of Zhixiang one million strings of cash to assist the rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, as Mingzong prepared the southern suburban sacrifice, he sent Li Renju to demand one million strings of cash from Zhixiang for the ceremony.

sentences.zh: 知祥覺唐謀欲困己，辭不肯出。

translations.literal: Zhixiang perceived that Tang plotted to distress him and declined, refusing to pay out.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixiang saw that the Tang court meant to squeeze him and refused to pay.

sentences.zh: 久之，請獻五十萬而已。

translations.literal: After a long time he asked to offer only five hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: After prolonged negotiation he offered only half a million.

sentences.zh: 初，魏王繼岌東歸，留精兵五千戍蜀。

translations.literal: At first, when Prince of Wei Jiji withdrew east, he left five thousand elite troops to garrison Shu.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Wei Jiji first withdrew eastward he had left five thousand elite troops to garrison Shu.

sentences.zh: 自安重誨疑知祥有異志，聽言事者，用己所親信分守兩川管內諸州，每除守將，則以精兵為其牙隊，多者二三千，少者不下五百人，以備緩急。

translations.literal: From the time An Chonghui suspected Zhixiang of a different intent, he listened to those who reported affairs and used his own trusted men to divide and guard the various prefectures within the two circuits' jurisdiction. Whenever a garrison commander was appointed, elite troops were made his headquarters guard—at most two or three thousand, at least no fewer than five hundred—to prepare for emergencies.
translations.idiomatic: Once An Chonghui suspected Zhixiang of disloyalty, he heeded informants and posted his own trusted men to hold prefectures throughout both circuits. Each new garrison commander received an elite headquarters guard—up to two or three thousand men, never fewer than five hundred—to meet emergencies.

sentences.zh: 是歲，以夏魯奇為武信軍節度使；

translations.literal: That year Xia Luqi was made military commissioner of the Martial Faith Army;
translations.idiomatic: That year Xia Luqi was appointed military commissioner of the Martial Faith Army;

sentences.zh: 分東川之閬州為保寧軍，以李仁矩為節度使；

translations.literal: Lang Prefecture of Eastern River was separated as the Tranquil Preservation Army, with Li Renju as military commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: Lang Prefecture was split from Eastern River as the Tranquil Preservation Army under Li Renju;

sentences.zh: 又以武虔裕為綿州刺史。

translations.literal: and Wu Qianyu was further made prefect of Mian.
translations.idiomatic: and Wu Qianyu was made prefect of Mian.

sentences.zh: 仁矩與東川董璋有隙，而虔裕重誨表兄，由是璋與知祥皆懼，以謂唐將致討。

translations.literal: Renju and Dong Zhang of Eastern River had a rift, while Qianyu was Chonghui's cousin on his mother's side; therefore Zhang and Zhixiang were both afraid and thought Tang would launch punitive action.
translations.idiomatic: Renju was at odds with Dong Zhang of Eastern River, while Qianyu was Chonghui's cousin on his mother's side. Zhang and Zhixiang alike grew fearful, believing the Tang court meant to move against them.

sentences.zh: 自璋鎮東川，未嘗與知祥通問，於是璋始遣人求婚以自結。

translations.literal: From the time Zhang governed Eastern River he had never exchanged messages with Zhixiang; thereupon Zhang first sent men to propose marriage to bind themselves together.
translations.idiomatic: Since taking command in Eastern River, Zhang had never exchanged messages with Zhixiang; he now sent envoys to propose a marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 而知祥心恨璋，欲不許，以問趙季良，季良以為宜合從以拒唐，知祥乃許。

translations.literal: But Zhixiang inwardly resented Zhang and wished not to agree; he asked Zhao Jiliang, who thought they should unite to resist Tang, and Zhixiang then agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixiang inwardly resented Zhang and was inclined to refuse, but when he asked Zhao Jiliang, Jiliang urged a joint stand against Tang, and Zhixiang consented.

sentences.zh: 於是連表請罷還唐所遣節度使、刺史等。

translations.literal: Thereupon they jointly memorialized asking to dismiss and return the military commissioners, prefects, and others sent by Tang.
translations.idiomatic: They then submitted joint memorials demanding withdrawal of the military commissioners and prefects the Tang court had posted to their circuits.

sentences.zh: 明宗優詔慰諭之。

translations.literal: Mingzong issued a gracious edict to console and instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong replied with a gracious edict of reassurance.

sentences.zh: 長興元年二月，明宗有事於南郊，加拜知祥中書令。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Changxing, when Mingzong performed the southern suburban sacrifice, he further invested Zhixiang as Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the first year of Changxing, when Mingzong performed the southern suburban sacrifice, he further promoted Zhixiang to Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 初，知祥與璋俱有異志，而重誨信言事者，以璋盡忠於國，獨知祥可疑，重誨猶欲倚璋以圖知祥。

translations.literal: At first Zhixiang and Zhang both had different intents, but Chonghui trusted those who reported affairs and regarded Zhang as wholly loyal to the state while Zhixiang alone was suspect; Chonghui still wished to rely on Zhang to scheme against Zhixiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixiang and Zhang had both harbored rebellious intent, but Chonghui trusted informants who called Zhang wholly loyal and Zhixiang alone suspect; he still hoped to use Zhang against Zhixiang.

sentences.zh: 是歲九月，董璋先反，攻破閬州，擒李仁矩殺之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of that year Dong Zhang rebelled first, stormed Lang Prefecture, captured Li Renju, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: That ninth month Dong Zhang rose first, stormed Lang Prefecture, captured Li Renju, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 是月應聖節，知祥開宴，東北望再拜，俯伏嗚咽，泣下沾襟，士卒皆為之歔欷，明日遂舉兵反。

translations.literal: That month was the Sacred Response Festival; Zhixiang held a banquet, bowed twice toward the northeast, prostrated himself sobbing, and tears soaked his robe; the soldiers all sighed and wept for him, and the next day he raised troops in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: That month, on the Sacred Response Festival, Zhixiang held a banquet, bowed twice toward the northeast, and prostrated himself in sobs until tears soaked his robe. The troops wept with him, and the next day he took up arms in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 是秋，明宗改封瓊華公主為福慶長公主，有司言前世公主受封，皆未出降，無遣使就藩冊命之儀。

translations.literal: That autumn Mingzong changed Princess Qionghua's title to Princess of Long Felicity; the officials said that in former ages when princesses received investiture they had not yet gone out in marriage, and there was no ritual of sending envoys to the fief to confer the patent.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Mingzong changed Princess Qionghua's title to Princess of Long Felicity. The officials noted that in earlier ages princesses had been enfeoffed before marriage and that no precedent existed for sending envoys to a husband's domain to confer the patent.

sentences.zh: 詔有司草具新儀，乃遣秘書監劉嶽為冊使。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the officials to draft new ritual procedures; then Secretary Director Liu Yue was sent as investiture envoy.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered officials to draft new ritual forms and sent Secretary Director Liu Yue as investiture envoy.

sentences.zh: 嶽行至鳳翔，聞知祥反，乃旋。

translations.literal: Yue traveled as far as Fengxiang, heard that Zhixiang had rebelled, and turned back.
translations.idiomatic: Yue reached Fengxiang, heard of Zhixiang's rebellion, and turned back.

sentences.zh: 明宗下詔削奪知祥官爵，命天雄軍節度使石敬瑭為都招討使，夏魯奇為副。

translations.literal: Mingzong issued an edict stripping Zhixiang of office and rank and appointed Tianxiong military commissioner Shi Jingtang as overall Pacification Commissioner with Xia Luqi as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong stripped Zhixiang of rank and office by edict and appointed Tianxiong military commissioner Shi Jingtang overall Pacification Commissioner with Xia Luqi as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 知祥遣李仁罕、張業、趙廷隱將兵三萬人會璋攻遂州，別遣侯弘實將四千人助璋守東川，又遣張武下峽取渝州。

translations.literal: Zhixiang sent Li Renhan, Zhang Ye, and Zhao Tingyin to lead thirty thousand troops to join Zhang in attacking Suizhou; separately he sent Hou Hongshi with four thousand to help Zhang hold Eastern River, and also sent Zhang Wu down the gorges to take Yu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixiang sent Li Renhan, Zhang Ye, and Zhao Tingyin with thirty thousand men to join Zhang in attacking Suizhou, dispatched Hou Hongshi with four thousand to help hold Eastern River, and sent Zhang Wu through the gorges to seize Yu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 唐師攻劍門，殺璋守兵三千人，遂入劍門。

translations.literal: Tang troops attacked Sword Gate, killed three thousand of Zhang's garrison troops, and then entered Sword Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Tang forces attacked Sword Gate, killed three thousand of Zhang's garrison troops, and broke through.

sentences.zh: 璋來告急，知祥大駭，遣廷隱分兵萬人以東，已而聞唐軍止劍州不進，喜曰：「使唐軍急趨東川，則遂州解圍，吾勢沮而兩川搖矣。

translations.literal: Zhang came reporting urgency; Zhixiang was greatly alarmed and sent Tingyin with ten thousand divided troops east. Before long he heard Tang troops halted at Sword Prefecture and did not advance. He rejoiced and said: "If Tang troops hurried toward Eastern River, then Suizhou would be relieved from siege, my momentum would be checked, and both circuits would be shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang sent urgent word for help. Zhixiang was alarmed and sent Tingyin east with ten thousand men. Soon he learned the Tang army had halted at Sword Prefecture. He rejoiced and said: "Had Tang forces rushed on Eastern River, Suizhou would have been relieved, my momentum broken, and both circuits thrown into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 今其不進，吾知易與爾。

translations.literal: Now that they do not advance, I know they are easy to deal with."
translations.idiomatic: Now that they hold back, I know they will be easy to handle."

sentences.zh: 」十二月，敬瑭及廷隱戰於劍門，唐師大敗。

translations.literal: " In the twelfth month Jingtang and Tingyin fought at Sword Gate; Tang troops were greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: " In the twelfth month Jingtang and Tingyin fought at Sword Gate and routed the Tang army.

sentences.zh: 張武已取渝州，武病卒，其副將袁彥超代將其軍，又取黔州。

translations.literal: Zhang Wu had already taken Yu Prefecture; Wu died of illness, and his deputy Yuan Yanchao took command of the army and also took Qian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wu had already taken Yu Prefecture; when Wu died of illness his deputy Yuan Yanchao assumed command and seized Qian Prefecture as well.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，李仁罕克遂州，夏魯奇死之，知祥以仁罕為武信軍留後，遣人馳魯奇首示敬瑭軍，敬瑭乃班師。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year Li Renhan captured Suizhou; Xia Luqi died in the fighting. Zhixiang made Renhan acting regent of the Martial Faith Army and sent men racing Luqi's head to display to Jingtang's army; Jingtang then withdrew his troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year Li Renhan took Suizhou and Xia Luqi was killed. Zhixiang made Renhan acting regent of the Martial Faith Army and sent Luqi's head posthaste to Jingtang's camp; Jingtang then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 利州李彥珂聞唐軍敗東歸，乃棄城走，知祥以趙廷隱為昭武軍留後。

translations.literal: Li Yanke of Lizhou, hearing Tang troops were defeated and returning east, abandoned the city and fled; Zhixiang made Zhao Tingyin acting regent of the Illustrious Martial Army.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yanke of Lizhou, hearing the Tang army had been beaten and was withdrawing east, abandoned the city and fled. Zhixiang made Zhao Tingyin acting regent of the Illustrious Martial Army.

sentences.zh: 李仁罕進攻夔州，刺史安崇阮棄城走，以趙季良為留後。

translations.literal: Li Renhan advanced to attack Kui Prefecture; prefect An Chongruan abandoned the city and fled; Zhao Jiliang was made acting regent.
translations.idiomatic: Li Renhan pressed the attack on Kui Prefecture; prefect An Chongruan fled, and Zhao Jiliang was made acting regent.

sentences.zh: 是時，唐軍涉險，以餉道為艱，自潼關以西，民苦轉饋，每費一石不能致一斗，道路嗟怨，而敬瑭軍亦旋，所在守將又皆棄城走。

translations.literal: At that time Tang troops crossed dangerous terrain and found supply routes arduous; from Tong Pass west the people suffered from transport levies—often spending a stone's cost to deliver no more than a dou—and the roads resounded with lament. Jingtang's army also withdrew, and garrison commanders everywhere abandoned their cities and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Tang troops were struggling through difficult terrain with supply lines stretched thin. West of Tong Pass the people groaned under transport levies—often paying the cost of a full stone of grain to move a single dou—and the roads filled with complaint. Jingtang's army withdrew as well, and garrison commanders everywhere abandoned their posts and fled.

sentences.zh: 明宗憂之，以責安重誨。

translations.literal: Mingzong was troubled by this and blamed An Chonghui.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong was deeply troubled and held An Chonghui responsible.

sentences.zh: 重誨懼，遽自請行。

translations.literal: Chonghui was afraid and hastily asked to go in person.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui, alarmed, promptly volunteered to go himself.

sentences.zh: 而重誨亦以被讒得罪死。

translations.literal: But Chonghui also, because of slander, was found guilty and died.
translations.idiomatic: But Chonghui was also destroyed by slander and put to death.

sentences.zh: 明宗謂致知祥等反，由重誨失策，及重誨死，乃遣西川進奏官蘇願、進奉軍將杜紹本西歸招諭知祥，具言知祥家屬在京師者皆無恙。

translations.literal: Mingzong said that Zhixiang and the others had rebelled because of Chonghui's mistaken policies; when Chonghui died he then sent Western River memorial officer Su Yuan and tribute-army officer Du Shaoben west to summon and instruct Zhixiang, stating in full that Zhixiang's family members in the capital were all unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong held that Zhixiang's rebellion stemmed from Chonghui's misjudgment. After Chonghui's death he sent Western River memorial officer Su Yuan and tribute-army officer Du Shaoben west to win Zhixiang over, assuring him that all his kin in the capital were safe.

sentences.zh: 知祥聞重誨誅死，而唐厚待其家屬，乃邀璋欲同謝罪，璋曰：「孟公家屬皆存，而我子孫獨見殺，我何謝為！

translations.literal: Zhixiang heard that Chonghui had been executed and that Tang treated his family generously; he then invited Zhang to submit guilt together. Zhang said: "Lord Meng's family members all survive, while my sons and grandsons alone were killed—what have I to submit for!
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of Chonghui's execution and the Tang court's generous treatment of his family, Zhixiang invited Zhang to submit a joint plea for pardon. Zhang said: "Your household is intact, Lord Meng, while my sons and grandsons were slaughtered—what have I to apologize for!

sentences.zh: 」知祥三遣使往見璋，璋不聽，乃遣觀察判官李昊說璋，璋益疑知祥賣己，因發怒，以語侵昊。

translations.literal: " Zhixiang three times sent envoys to visit Zhang; Zhang would not receive them. He then sent administrative aide Li Hao to persuade Zhang. Zhang grew more suspicious that Zhixiang was selling him out and therefore grew angry, using words that insulted Hao.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhixiang sent envoys three times; Zhang refused to see them. Zhixiang then sent administrative aide Li Hao to reason with him. Zhang grew more convinced Zhixiang meant to betray him, flew into a rage, and insulted Hao to his face.

sentences.zh: 昊乃勸知祥攻之。

translations.literal: Hao then urged Zhixiang to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Hao thereupon urged Zhixiang to attack him.

sentences.zh: 而璋先襲破知祥漢州，知祥遣趙廷隱率兵三萬，自將擊之，陣雞距橋。

translations.literal: But Zhang first raided and stormed Zhixiang's Han Prefecture. Zhixiang sent Zhao Tingyin with thirty thousand troops and personally led the attack, forming battle lines at Cock's Spur Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang struck first, overrunning Zhixiang's Han Prefecture. Zhixiang sent Zhao Tingyin with thirty thousand men and took the field himself, drawing up battle lines at Cock's Spur Bridge.

sentences.zh: 知祥得璋降卒，衣以錦袍，使持書招降璋，璋曰：「事已及此，不可悔也！

translations.literal: Zhixiang obtained Zhang's surrendered soldiers, clothed them in brocade robes, and had them carry letters to summon Zhang to surrender. Zhang said: "Matters have already reached this point—it cannot be regretted!
translations.idiomatic: Zhixiang took Zhang's surrendered troops, dressed them in brocade robes, and sent them with letters urging Zhang to yield. Zhang said: "Matters have gone too far for regret now!

sentences.zh: 」璋軍士皆噪曰：「徒曝我於日中，何不速戰？

translations.literal: " Zhang's soldiers all clamored, saying: "You merely expose us in the midday sun—why not fight quickly?
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang's soldiers clamored: "You leave us baking in the midday sun—why not fight at once?

sentences.zh: 」璋即麾軍以戰。

translations.literal: " Zhang immediately waved the army to battle.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang immediately ordered his army into battle.

sentences.zh: 兵始交，璋偏將張守進來降，知祥乘之，璋遂大敗，走。

translations.literal: As the troops first engaged, Zhang's flank general Zhang Shoujin came over in surrender; Zhixiang pressed the advantage, and Zhang was greatly defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: As battle was joined, Zhang's flank general Zhang Shoujin defected. Zhixiang pressed the advantage, and Zhang was routed and fled.

sentences.zh: 過金雁橋，麾其子光嗣使降，以保家族，光嗣哭曰：「自古豈有殺父以求生者乎，寧俱就死！

translations.literal: Passing Golden Goose Bridge, he waved his son Guangsi to surrender in order to preserve the clan. Guangsi wept and said: "Since antiquity has there ever been one who killed his father to seek life? Better that we die together!
translations.idiomatic: At Golden Goose Bridge he ordered his son Guangsi to surrender and save the family. Guangsi wept and said: "Since antiquity has any son killed his father to live? Let us die together!

sentences.zh: 」因與璋俱走。

translations.literal: " He therefore fled together with Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore fled together with his father.

sentences.zh: 知祥遣趙廷隱追之，不及，璋走至梓州見殺，光嗣自縊死，知祥遂並有東川。

translations.literal: Zhixiang sent Zhao Tingyin in pursuit but could not overtake them. Zhang fled to Zizhou and was killed on sight; Guangsi hanged himself. Zhixiang then possessed Eastern River as well.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixiang sent Zhao Tingyin in pursuit but could not catch them. Zhang reached Zizhou and was killed; Guangsi hanged himself. Zhixiang thereby gained control of Eastern River as well.

sentences.zh: 然自璋死，知祥卒不遣使謝唐。

translations.literal: Yet from Zhang's death onward, Zhixiang in the end never sent envoys to thank Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Yet after Zhang's death Zhixiang never sent envoys to thank the Tang court.

sentences.zh: 唐樞密使範延光曰：「知祥雖已破璋，必借朝廷之勢，以為兩川之重，自非屈意招之，彼亦不能自歸也。

translations.literal: Tang Chief Palace Secretary Fan Yanguang said: "Although Zhixiang has already defeated Zhang, he is certain to borrow the court's authority to make himself weighty in the two circuits. Unless we summon him with yielding intent, he also cannot return of himself.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Chief Palace Secretary Fan Yanguang said: "Though Zhixiang has defeated Zhang, he will surely lean on the court's authority to consolidate his hold on both circuits. Unless we woo him with deliberate humility, he will not come back on his own.

sentences.zh: 」明宗曰：「知祥，吾故人也，本因間諜致此危疑，撫吾故人，何屈意之有？

translations.literal: " Mingzong said: "Zhixiang is my old acquaintance. This danger and doubt arose originally because of spies and informers. To comfort my old acquaintance—what need is there to yield?
translations.idiomatic: " Mingzong said: "Zhixiang is an old friend. Spies and informers created this crisis. To comfort an old friend—where is the need for humility?

sentences.zh: 」先是，克寧妻孟氏，知祥妹也。

translations.literal: " Earlier, the wife of Kerning, Lady Meng, was Zhixiang's younger sister.
translations.idiomatic: " Earlier, the wife of Kerning—Lady Meng—was Zhixiang's younger sister.

sentences.zh: 莊宗已殺克寧，孟氏歸於知祥，其子瑰，留事唐為供奉官。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong had already killed Kerning; Lady Meng returned to Zhixiang. Her son Gui remained in Tang service as a palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong had executed Kerning; Lady Meng returned to Zhixiang. Her son Gui remained at the Tang court as a palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 明宗即遣瑰歸省其母，因賜知祥詔書招慰之。

translations.literal: Mingzong then sent Gui back to visit his mother and thereby bestowed on Zhixiang an edict summoning and comforting him.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong sent Gui home to visit his mother and with him an edict summoning and reassuring Zhixiang.

sentences.zh: 知祥兼據兩川，以趙季良為武泰軍留後、李仁罕武信軍留後、趙廷隱保寧軍留後、張業寧江軍留後、李肇昭武軍留後。

translations.literal: Zhixiang held both circuits together and made Zhao Jiliang acting regent of the Martial Grand Army, Li Renhan of the Martial Faith Army, Zhao Tingyin of the Tranquil Preservation Army, Zhang Ye of the Tranquil River Army, and Li Zhao of the Illustrious Martial Army.
translations.idiomatic: Holding both circuits, Zhixiang appointed Zhao Jiliang acting regent of the Martial Grand Army, Li Renhan of the Martial Faith Army, Zhao Tingyin of the Tranquil Preservation Army, Zhang Ye of the Tranquil River Army, and Li Zhao of the Illustrious Martial Army.

sentences.zh: 季良等因請知祥稱王，以墨制行事，議未決而瑰至蜀。

translations.literal: Jiliang and the others thereupon asked Zhixiang to declare himself king and conduct affairs by informal imperial writ; the deliberation was not settled when Gui reached Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Jiliang and the others urged Zhixiang to declare himself king and govern by informal imperial writ, but the matter was still undecided when Gui reached Shu.

sentences.zh: 知祥見瑰倨慢。

translations.literal: Zhixiang saw that Gui was arrogant and disrespectful.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixiang found Gui arrogant and disrespectful.

sentences.zh: 九月，瑰自蜀還，得知祥表，請除趙季良等為五鎮節度，其餘刺史已下，得自除授。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Gui returned from Shu and obtained Zhixiang's memorial, requesting that Zhao Jiliang and the others be appointed military commissioners of the five armies, while all others from prefect downward might be appointed by himself.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Gui returned from Shu with Zhixiang's memorial asking that Zhao Jiliang and the others be made military commissioners of the five armies and that all appointments from prefect downward be left to his own discretion.

sentences.zh: 又請封蜀王，且言福慶公主已卒。

translations.literal: He also asked to enfeoff him as King of Shu and reported that Princess of Long Felicity had died.
translations.idiomatic: He also requested enfeoffment as King of Shu and reported the death of the Princess of Long Felicity.

sentences.zh: 明宗為之發哀，遣閣門使劉政恩為宣諭使。

translations.literal: Mingzong proclaimed mourning for her and sent Gate Commissioner Liu Zheng'en as Instruction Envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong proclaimed mourning and sent Gate Commissioner Liu Zheng'en as Instruction Envoy.

sentences.zh: 政恩復命，知祥始遣其將朱滉來朝。

translations.literal: When Zheng'en returned from his mission, Zhixiang at last sent his general Zhu Huang to court.
translations.idiomatic: After Zheng'en reported back, Zhixiang at last sent his general Zhu Huang to court.

sentences.zh: 四年二月癸亥，制以知祥檢校太尉兼中書令，行成都尹、劍南東西兩川節度，管內觀察處置、統押近界諸蠻，兼西山八國雲南安撫制置等使。

translations.literal: On the guihai day of the second month of the fourth year, by imperial order Zhixiang was made Acting Grand Guardian and Director of the Secretariat, acting Chengdu Intendant, military commissioner of the Sword-South Eastern and Western circuits, with jurisdiction over observation and disposition within the circuit, overall command of the nearby border tribes, and concurrently Commissioner for Pacification and Disposition of the Eight Kingdoms of the Western Mountains and Yun'an.
translations.idiomatic: On the guihai day of the second month in the fourth year an edict named Zhixiang Acting Grand Guardian and Director of the Secretariat, acting Chengdu Intendant, military commissioner of both Sword-South circuits, with circuit-wide observation and disposition, overall command of neighboring border tribes, and concurrent commissioner for the Eight Kingdoms of the Western Mountains and Yun'an pacification.

sentences.zh: 遣工部尚書盧文紀冊封知祥為蜀王，而趙季良等五人皆拜節度使。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Lu Wenji was sent to invest Zhixiang as King of Shu, and Zhao Jiliang and the other five were all invested as military commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Lu Wenji was dispatched to invest Zhixiang as King of Shu, and Zhao Jiliang and the other four were all appointed military commissioners.

sentences.zh: 唐兵先在蜀者數萬人，知祥皆厚給其衣食，因請送其家屬，明宗詔諭不許。

translations.literal: Several tens of thousands of Tang troops were already in Shu; Zhixiang generously supplied their food and clothing and therefore asked to send their families back. Mingzong issued an edict of instruction refusing permission.
translations.idiomatic: Several tens of thousands of Tang troops remained in Shu; Zhixiang generously supplied their food and clothing and asked permission to send their families home, but Mingzong refused by edict.

sentences.zh: 十一月，明宗崩。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Mingzong died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Mingzong died.

sentences.zh: 明年閏正月，知祥乃即皇帝位，國號蜀。

translations.literal: In the intercalary first month of the following year Zhixiang then took the imperial throne; the state was named Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary first month of the following year Zhixiang proclaimed himself emperor and named his state Shu.

sentences.zh: 以趙季良為司空、同中書門下平章事，中門使王處回為樞密使，李昊為翰林學士。

translations.literal: Zhao Jiliang was made Minister of Works and Associate Director of the Secretariat; Inner Gate Commissioner Wang Chuhui was made Chief Palace Secretary; Li Hao was made Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: He made Zhao Jiliang Minister of Works and Associate Director of the Secretariat, Inner Gate Commissioner Wang Chuhui Chief Palace Secretary, and Li Hao Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 三月，唐潞王舉兵於鳳翔，湣帝遣王思同等討之，思同兵潰，山南西道節度使張虔釗、武定軍節度使孫漢韶皆以其地附於蜀。

translations.literal: In the third month the Tang Prince of Lu raised troops at Fengxiang; Emperor Min sent Wang Sitong and others to attack him. Sitong's army collapsed, and Southern Mountain Western Circuit military commissioner Zhang Qianzhao and Martial Settlement Army military commissioner Sun Hanshao both attached their territories to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the Tang Prince of Lu rebelled at Fengxiang. Emperor Min sent Wang Sitong against him, but Sitong's army collapsed. Southern Mountain Western Circuit commissioner Zhang Qianzhao and Martial Settlement commissioner Sun Hanshao both submitted their territories to Shu.

sentences.zh: 四月，知祥改元曰明德。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Zhixiang changed the reign title to Bright Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Zhixiang adopted the reign title Bright Virtue.

sentences.zh: 六月，虔釗等至成都，知祥宴勞之，虔釗奉觴起為壽，知祥手緩不能舉觴，遂病，以其子昶為皇太子監國。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Qianzhao and the others reached Chengdu; Zhixiang feasted and rewarded them. Qianzhao raised his cup to offer a toast for long life, but Zhixiang's hand was slow and could not lift the cup; he then fell ill and made his son Chang crown prince to oversee the state.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Qianzhao and the others reached Chengdu, where Zhixiang feasted them. Qianzhao rose with a cup to toast his health, but Zhixiang's hand trembled and he could not raise his cup. He fell ill and made his son Chang crown prince regent.

sentences.zh: 知祥卒，謚為文武聖德英烈明孝皇帝，廟號高祖，陵曰和陵。

translations.literal: Zhixiang died. His posthumous title was Civil and Martial Sage of Virtue, Heroic and Illustrious, Bright and Filial Emperor; his temple name was High Ancestor; his tomb was called Harmonious Tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixiang died. He was posthumously titled Civil and Martial Sage of Virtue, Heroic and Illustrious, Bright and Filial Emperor; his temple name was High Ancestor; his tomb was called Harmonious Tomb.

sentences.zh: 昶，知祥第三子也。

translations.literal: Chang was Zhixiang's third son.
translations.idiomatic: Chang was Zhixiang's third son.

sentences.zh: 知祥為兩川節度使，昶為行軍司馬。

translations.literal: When Zhixiang was military commissioner of the two circuits, Chang was campaigning marshal.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhixiang held both river circuits, Chang served as campaigning marshal.

sentences.zh: 知祥僭號，以昶為東川節度使、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: When Zhixiang usurped the imperial title, he made Chang military commissioner of Eastern River and Associate Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhixiang declared himself emperor, he made Chang military commissioner of Eastern River and Associate Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 知祥病，昶監國。

translations.literal: When Zhixiang fell ill, Chang oversaw the state.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhixiang fell ill, Chang served as regent.

sentences.zh: 知祥已卒而秘未發，王處回夜過趙季良，相對泣涕不已，季良正色曰：「今強侯握兵，專伺時變，當速立嗣君以絕非望，泣無益也。

translations.literal: Zhixiang had already died but the news was kept secret and not released. Wang Chuhui visited Zhao Jiliang by night; facing each other they wept without end. Jiliang said sternly: "Now powerful lords hold troops and watch exclusively for changing times. You should quickly establish the heir to cut off vain hopes—weeping is of no use.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixiang was dead but the news had not yet been announced. Wang Chuhui visited Zhao Jiliang at night, and they wept together without end. Jiliang said sternly: "Powerful lords now hold armies and watch for any opening. Establish the heir at once to forestall ambition—tears will not help.

sentences.zh: 」處回遂與季良立昶，而後發喪。

translations.literal: " Chuhui then joined Jiliang in establishing Chang, and only afterward announced the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: " Chuhui and Jiliang thereupon installed Chang and only then announced the mourning.

sentences.zh: 昶立，不改元，仍稱明德，至五年始改元曰慶政。

translations.literal: When Chang took the throne he did not change the reign title and still called it Bright Virtue; only in the fifth year did he change the reign title to Celebrated Governance.
translations.idiomatic: On his accession Chang kept the reign title Bright Virtue; only in his fifth year did he change it to Celebrated Governance.

sentences.zh: 明德三年三月，熒惑犯積屍，昶以謂積屍蜀分也，懼，欲禳之，以問司天少監胡韞，韞曰：「按十二次，起井五度至柳八度，為鶉首之次，鶉首，秦分也，蜀雖屬秦，乃極南之表爾。

translations.literal: In the third month of the third year of Bright Virtue, the Sparkling Deluder invaded the Heap of Corpses; Chang thought the Heap of Corpses was Shu territory and was afraid, wishing to perform expiation. He asked Vice Director of Astronomy Hu Yun, who said: "According to the twelve stations, from five degrees in Well to eight degrees in Willow is the station of Quail's Head. Quail's Head is Qin territory. Although Shu belongs to Qin, it is only the extreme southern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the third year of Bright Virtue the Sparkling Deluder invaded the Heap of Corpses. Chang took this as a sign for Shu and grew fearful, wishing to perform expiatory rites. He asked Vice Director of Astronomy Hu Yun, who said: "By the twelve celestial stations, from five degrees in Well to eight degrees in Willow lies Quail's Head—Qin territory. Shu belongs to Qin only in the sense that it lies at Qin's far southern edge.

sentences.zh: 前世火入鬼，其應在秦。

translations.literal: In former ages when fire entered the Ghost, the omen fell on Qin.
translations.idiomatic: In earlier ages, when fire entered the Ghost, the omen struck Qin.

sentences.zh: 晉咸和九年三月，火犯積屍，四月，雍州刺史郭權見殺。

translations.literal: In the third month of the ninth year of Xiande of Jin, fire invaded the Heap of Corpses; in the fourth month Yong Prefecture inspector Guo Quan was killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the ninth year of Xiande under Jin, fire invaded the Heap of Corpses; in the fourth month Guo Quan, inspector of Yong Prefecture, was killed.

sentences.zh: 義熙四年，火犯鬼，明年，雍州刺史朱齡石見殺。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yixi, fire invaded the Ghost; the next year Yong Prefecture inspector Zhu Lingshi was killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yixi fire invaded the Ghost; the following year Zhu Lingshi, inspector of Yong Prefecture, was killed.

sentences.zh: 而蜀皆無事。

translations.literal: Yet Shu was always unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Shu each time escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: " He then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " Chang then abandoned the idea.

sentences.zh: 昶好打球走馬，又為方士房中之術，多采良家子以充後宮。

translations.literal: Chang loved ball games and horse racing, and also practiced the chamber arts of Daoist masters, taking many daughters of good families to fill the rear palace.
translations.idiomatic: Chang loved polo and horse racing and practiced the bedroom arts of Daoist masters, taking many daughters of respectable families into the rear palace.

sentences.zh: 樞密副使韓保貞切諫，昶大悟，即日出之，賜保貞金數斤。

translations.literal: Deputy Chief Palace Secretary Han Baozhen remonstrated urgently; Chang was greatly awakened, released them the same day, and bestowed on Baozhen several jin of gold.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy Chief Palace Secretary Han Baozhen remonstrated sharply. Chang took the lesson to heart, released the women the same day, and rewarded Baozhen with several jin of gold.

sentences.zh: 有上書者，言臺省官當擇清流，昶嘆曰：「何不言擇其人而任之？

translations.literal: Someone submitted a memorial saying that officials of the Secretariat and Censorate should be chosen from the pure current. Chang sighed and said: "Why not say choose the man and employ him?
translations.idiomatic: A memorial arrived arguing that Secretariat and Censorate posts should go only to men of pure pedigree. Chang sighed and said: "Why not say choose the right man for the post?

sentences.zh: 」左右請以其言詰上書者，昶曰：「吾見唐太宗初即位，獄吏孫伏伽上書言事，皆見嘉納，奈何勸我拒諫耶！」

translations.literal: " Those at his side asked to use his words to rebuke the memorial writer. Chang said: "I have seen that when Emperor Taizong of Tang first took the throne, the prison clerk Sun Fugai submitted memorials on affairs and all were praised and accepted—how can you urge me to reject remonstrance!"
translations.idiomatic: " His attendants urged him to use these words to rebuke the memorialist. Chang said: "I recall that when Emperor Taizong of Tang first took the throne, the prison clerk Sun Fugai submitted memorials on public affairs and all were welcomed—how can you urge me to shut out remonstrance!"

sentences.zh: 然昶年少不親政事，而將相大臣皆知祥故人，知祥寬厚，多優縱之，及其事昶，益驕蹇，多逾法度，務廣第宅，奪人良田，發其墳墓，而李仁罕、張業尤甚。

translations.literal: Yet Chang was young and did not attend to government affairs, while the generals and chief ministers were all Zhixiang's old associates. Zhixiang had been generous and broad, and mostly indulged them leniently. When they served Chang they grew still more arrogant and obstructive, often exceeding the law, striving to enlarge their mansions, seizing others' fertile fields, and opening their graves—and Li Renhan and Zhang Ye were especially extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Chang was young and left government largely to others. His generals and chief ministers were Zhixiang's old companions; Zhixiang had been indulgent with them, and under Chang they grew still more arrogant and lawless, enlarging their mansions, seizing fertile land, and opening graves—Li Renhan and Zhang Ye worst of all.

sentences.zh: 昶即位數月，執仁罕殺之，並族其家。

translations.literal: Several months after Chang took the throne he seized Renhan and killed him, exterminating his clan as well.
translations.idiomatic: Within months of his accession Chang seized Renhan and executed him, exterminating his entire clan.

sentences.zh: 是時，李肇自鎮來朝，杖而入見，稱疾不拜，及聞仁罕死，遽釋杖而拜。

translations.literal: At that time Li Zhao came from his command to court, entered leaning on a staff, claimed illness and did not bow; when he heard Renhan was dead he hastily dropped the staff and bowed.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Zhao came to court from his command leaning on a staff, claiming illness and refusing to bow. When he heard Renhan was dead he promptly dropped the staff and bowed.

sentences.zh: 廣政九年，趙季良卒，張業益用事。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Broad Governance Zhao Jiliang died, and Zhang Ye wielded power all the more.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Broad Governance Zhao Jiliang died, and Zhang Ye's influence grew.

sentences.zh: 業，仁罕甥也。

translations.literal: Ye was Renhan's nephew on his mother's side.
translations.idiomatic: Ye was Renhan's nephew.

sentences.zh: 仁罕被誅時，業方掌禁兵，昶懼其反，乃用以為相，業兼判度支，置獄於家，務以酷法厚斂蜀人，蜀人大怨。

translations.literal: When Renhan was executed Ye was in charge of the forbidden troops; Chang feared he would rebel and therefore used him as chief minister. Ye concurrently oversaw the Revenue Bureau, set up a prison in his home, and strove to enrich himself from the people of Shu by harsh laws; the people of Shu greatly resented him.
translations.idiomatic: When Renhan was executed Ye still commanded the palace guard. Fearing rebellion, Chang made him chief minister. Ye also oversaw the Revenue Bureau, maintained a private prison, and squeezed the people of Shu with harsh laws until they bitterly resented him.

sentences.zh: 十一年，昶與匡聖指揮使安思謙謀，執而殺之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Chang plotted with Upright Sage Command Commissioner An Siqian, seized him, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Chang plotted with Upright Sage Command Commissioner An Siqian, seized Ye, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 王處回、趙廷隱相次致仕，由是故將舊臣殆盡。

translations.literal: Wang Chuhui and Zhao Tingyin successively retired from office; thereby the former generals and old ministers were nearly all gone.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chuhui and Zhao Tingyin retired in succession, and with them nearly all of Zhixiang's old generals and ministers were gone.

sentences.zh: 昶始親政事，於朝堂置匭以通下情。

translations.literal: Chang at last attended to government affairs himself and set up a complaint box in the court hall to communicate the feelings of those below.
translations.idiomatic: Chang at last took up government himself and placed a complaint box in the court hall to hear from the people.

sentences.zh: 是時，契丹滅晉，漢高祖起於太原，中國多故，雄武軍節度使何建以秦、成、階三州附於蜀，昶因遣孫漢韶攻下鳳州，於是悉有王衍故地。

translations.literal: At that time the Khitan destroyed Jin and Han Gaozu rose at Taiyuan; the central lands had many troubles. Heroic Martial Army military commissioner He Jian attached Qin, Cheng, and Jie prefectures to Shu. Chang thereupon sent Sun Hanshao to storm Feng Prefecture, and thereby possessed all of Wang Yan's former territory.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan had destroyed Jin and Han Gaozu had risen at Taiyuan; the central plains were in turmoil. Heroic Martial commissioner He Jian submitted Qin, Cheng, and Jie prefectures to Shu. Chang sent Sun Hanshao to take Feng Prefecture and thereby recovered all of Wang Yan's former territory.

sentences.zh: 漢將趙思綰據永興、王景崇據鳳翔反，皆送款於昶。

translations.literal: Han generals Zhao Sixuan held Yongxing and Wang Jingchong held Fengxiang in rebellion; both sent pledges of allegiance to Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Han generals Zhao Sixuan at Yongxing and Wang Jingchong at Fengxiang rebelled and both offered their allegiance to Chang.

sentences.zh: 昶遣張虔釗出大散關，何建出隴右，李廷珪出子午谷，以應思綰。

translations.literal: Chang sent Zhang Qianzhao out through Great Scatter Pass, He Jian out through the Longyou region, and Li Tinggui out through Ziwu Valley to respond to Sixuan.
translations.idiomatic: Chang sent Zhang Qianzhao through Great Scatter Pass, He Jian through the Longyou region, and Li Tinggui through Ziwu Valley to support Sixuan.

sentences.zh: 昶相母昭裔切諫，以為不可，然昶誌欲窺關中甚銳，乃遣安思謙益兵以東。

translations.literal: Chancellor Mu Zhaoyi remonstrated urgently, thinking it could not be done, but Chang's will to peer into the Guanzhong region was very keen, and he therefore sent An Siqian with added troops east.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Mu Zhaoyi remonstrated sharply that the move was unwise, but Chang was eager to probe the Guanzhong region and sent An Siqian east with reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 已而漢誅思綰、景崇，虔釗等皆罷歸，而思謙恥於無功，多殺士卒以威眾。

translations.literal: Before long Han executed Sixuan and Jingchong; Qianzhao and the others all withdrew and returned, while Siqian, ashamed at achieving nothing, killed many soldiers to awe the masses.
translations.idiomatic: Han soon executed Sixuan and Jingchong, and Qianzhao and the others withdrew. Siqian, shamed by his failure, killed many soldiers to intimidate his men.

sentences.zh: 昶與翰林使王藻謀殺思謙，而邊吏有急奏，藻不以時聞，輒啟其封，昶怒之。

translations.literal: Chang plotted with Hanlin envoy Wang Zao to kill Siqian. A frontier official had an urgent memorial, but Zao did not report it in time and opened its seal on his own; Chang was angry at him.
translations.idiomatic: Chang plotted with Hanlin envoy Wang Zao to kill Siqian. When an urgent frontier report arrived, Zao failed to forward it promptly and opened the seal himself; Chang was furious.

sentences.zh: 其殺思謙也，藻方侍側，因並擒藻斬之。

translations.literal: When he killed Siqian, Zao was attending at his side; he therefore seized Zao as well and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: When Siqian was killed, Zao was attending at his side and was seized and beheaded as well.

sentences.zh: 十二年，置吏部三銓、禮部貢舉。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he established the three boards of the Ministry of Personnel and the Ministry of Rites examination for recruitment.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he established the three selection boards of the Ministry of Personnel and civil-service examinations under the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 十三年，昶加號睿文英武仁聖明孝皇帝。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Chang added the title Sagacious in Culture, Heroic in Martial Affairs, Benevolent and Sage, Bright and Filial Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Chang added the honorific Sagacious in Culture, Heroic in Martial Affairs, Benevolent and Sage, Bright and Filial Emperor.

sentences.zh: 封子玄喆秦王，判六軍事；

translations.literal: His son Xuanzhe was enfeoffed as Prince of Qin and assigned the six armies;
translations.idiomatic: His son Xuanzhe was enfeoffed Prince of Qin and given command of the six armies;

sentences.zh: 次子玄玨褒王；

translations.literal: the second son Xuanjue as Prince of Bao;
translations.idiomatic: the second son Xuanjue as Prince of Bao;

sentences.zh: 弟仁毅夔王，仁贄雅王，仁裕嘉王。

translations.literal: his younger brothers Renyi as Prince of Kui, Renzan as Prince of Ya, and Renyu as Prince of Jia.
translations.idiomatic: his younger brothers Renyi as Prince of Kui, Renzan as Prince of Ya, and Renyu as Prince of Jia.

sentences.zh: 十八年，周世宗伐蜀，攻自秦州。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year Emperor Shizong of Zhou attacked Shu, advancing from Qin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year Emperor Shizong of Zhou attacked Shu from Qin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 昶以韓繼勛為雄武軍節度，聞周師來伐，嘆曰：「繼勛豈足以當周兵邪！

translations.literal: Chang made Han Jixun military commissioner of the Heroic Martial Army. Hearing Zhou troops were coming to attack, he sighed and said: "Can Jixun really stand against Zhou troops!
translations.idiomatic: Chang appointed Han Jixun military commissioner of the Heroic Martial Army. Hearing that Zhou forces were advancing, he sighed: "Can Jixun really stand against the Zhou army!

sentences.zh: 」客省使趙季劄請行，乃以季劄為秦州監軍使。

translations.literal: " Guest Reception Commissioner Zhao Jizha asked to go, and he was therefore made army supervisor of Qin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: " Guest Reception Commissioner Zhao Jizha volunteered to go, and Chang made him army supervisor at Qin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 季劄行至德陽，聞周兵至，遽馳還奏事。

translations.literal: Jizha traveled as far as Deyang, heard Zhou troops had arrived, and hastily raced back to report.
translations.idiomatic: Jizha reached Deyang, heard Zhou troops had arrived, and raced back to report.

sentences.zh: 昶問之，季劄惶懼不能道一言，昶怒殺之，乃遣高彥儔、李廷珪出堂倉以拒周師。

translations.literal: Chang questioned him; Jizha was fearful and could not speak a single word. Chang angrily killed him and then sent Gao Yanchou and Li Tinggui out from Tang Granary to resist Zhou troops.
translations.idiomatic: Chang questioned him, but Jizha was too terrified to speak. Chang had him executed and sent Gao Yanchou and Li Tinggui out from Tang Granary to resist the Zhou army.

sentences.zh: 彥儔大敗，走青泥，於是秦、成、階、鳳復入於周。

translations.literal: Yanchou was greatly defeated and fled to Green Mud; thereupon Qin, Cheng, Jie, and Feng returned to Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yanchou was routed and fled to Green Mud, and Qin, Cheng, Jie, and Feng fell back to Zhou control.

sentences.zh: 昶懼，分遣使者聘於南唐、東漢，以張形勢。

translations.literal: Chang was afraid and separately sent envoys to court Southern Tang and Eastern Han to display his strength.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed, Chang sent envoys to Southern Tang and Eastern Han to display his strength.

sentences.zh: 二十年，世宗以所得蜀俘歸之，昶亦歸所獲周將胡立於京師，因寓書於世宗，世宗怒昶無臣禮，不答。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year Shizong returned the Shu captives he had obtained; Chang also returned the Zhou general Hu Li he had captured to the capital and thereby sent a letter enclosed to Shizong. Shizong was angry that Chang lacked the ritual of a subject and did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year Shizong returned the Shu captives he had taken. Chang sent back the Zhou general Hu Li and enclosed a letter to Shizong, who, angered by Chang's lack of subject ritual, did not reply.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，周兵伐南唐，取淮南十四州，諸國皆懼。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year Zhou troops attacked Southern Tang and took fourteen prefectures in Huainan; all states were afraid.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year Zhou forces attacked Southern Tang and seized fourteen Huainan prefectures, and every neighboring state grew fearful.

sentences.zh: 荊南高保融以書招昶使歸周，昶以前嘗致書世宗不答，乃止。

translations.literal: Southern Jing's Gao Baorong sent a letter inviting Chang to submit to Zhou, but Chang, because he had earlier sent a letter to Shizong without reply, then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Baorong of Southern Jing wrote inviting Chang to submit to Zhou, but Chang, remembering Shizong's silence to his earlier letter, let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 昶幼子玄寶，生七歲而卒，太常言無服之殤無贈典，昶問李昊，昊曰：「昔唐德宗皇子評生四歲而卒，贈揚州大都督，封肅王，此故事也。

translations.literal: Chang's youngest son Xuanbao was born and died at seven years. The Court of Imperial Sacrifices said that a child who died without having worn mourning garments had no posthumous honors. Chang asked Li Hao, who said: "Formerly under Tang Dezong the imperial son Ping was born and died at four years; he was posthumously made Grand Governor of Yang Prefecture and enfeoffed as Prince of Su—this is precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Chang's youngest son Xuanbao died at seven. The Court of Imperial Sacrifices said a child who died before wearing mourning had no posthumous honors. Chang asked Li Hao, who said: "Under Tang Dezong the imperial son Ping died at four and was posthumously made Grand Governor of Yang Prefecture and enfeoffed Prince of Su—that is precedent.

sentences.zh: 」昶乃贈玄寶青州大都督，追封遂王。

translations.literal: " Chang then posthumously made Xuanbao Grand Governor of Qing Prefecture and enfeoffed him as Prince of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: " Chang thereupon posthumously made Xuanbao Grand Governor of Qing Prefecture and enfeoffed him as Prince of Sui.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，立秦王玄喆為皇太子。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he established Prince of Qin Xuanzhe as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he made Prince of Qin Xuanzhe crown prince.

sentences.zh: 昶幸晉、漢之際，中國多故，而據險一方，君臣務為奢侈以自娛，至於溺器，皆以七寶裝之。

translations.literal: Chang was fortunate in the interval between Jin and Han; the central lands had many troubles while he held a perilous corner alone. Ruler and ministers strove for luxury to amuse themselves—even chamber pots were adorned with the seven treasures.
translations.idiomatic: Chang was fortunate to reign while Jin and Han collapsed and the central plains were in chaos, holding a secure corner apart. Court and ministers devoted themselves to luxury—even their chamber pots were set with the seven treasures.

sentences.zh: 宋興，已下荊、潭，昶益懼，遣大程官孫遇以蠟丸書間行東漢，約出兵以撓中國，遇為邊吏所得。

translations.literal: When Song arose it had already taken Jing and Tan; Chang grew still more afraid and sent Senior Process Officer Sun Yu with a wax-sealed letter traveling secretly to Eastern Han to arrange troops to harass the central lands. Yu was seized by frontier officials.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song rose and took Jing and Tan, Chang grew more fearful and sent Senior Process Officer Sun Yu with a wax-sealed letter through secret routes to Eastern Han to arrange a diversion against the central plains. Yu was captured by frontier officials.

sentences.zh: 太祖皇帝遂詔伐蜀，遣王全斌、崔彥進等出鳳州，劉光乂、曹彬等出歸州；

translations.literal: The founding emperor then issued an edict to attack Shu, sending Wang Quanbin, Cui Yanjin, and others out from Feng Prefecture and Liu Guangyi, Cao Bin, and others out from Gui Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor then ordered an attack on Shu, sending Wang Quanbin and Cui Yanjin out from Feng Prefecture and Liu Guangyi and Cao Bin out from Gui Prefecture;

sentences.zh: 詔八作司度右掖門南、臨汴水為昶治第一區，凡五百餘間，供帳什物皆具，以待昶。

translations.literal: an edict ordered the Eight Works Bureau to measure south of the Right Flank Gate beside the Bian River and build Chang a first-class residence of more than five hundred rooms, with supplies and furnishings all complete, to await Chang.
translations.idiomatic: and ordered the Eight Works Bureau to build south of the Right Flank Gate on the Bian River a first-class residence of more than five hundred rooms, fully furnished, to await Chang's arrival.

sentences.zh: 昶遣王昭遠、趙彥韜等拒命。

translations.literal: Chang sent Wang Zhaoyuan, Zhao Yantao, and others to resist the command.
translations.idiomatic: Chang sent Wang Zhaoyuan, Zhao Yantao, and others to resist.

sentences.zh: 昭遠，成都人也，年十三，事東郭禪師智諲為童子。

translations.literal: Zhaoyuan was a man of Chengdu. At thirteen he served the Chan master Zhiyun of East Suburb as a novice.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoyuan was from Chengdu. At thirteen he became a novice under the Chan master Zhiyun of East Suburb.

sentences.zh: 知祥嘗飯僧於府，昭遠執巾履從智諲以入，知祥見之，愛其惠黠。

translations.literal: Zhixiang once fed monks at his residence; Zhaoyuan carried towel and shoes following Zhiyun inside. Zhixiang saw him and loved his cleverness.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhixiang once entertained monks at his residence, Zhaoyuan followed Zhiyun in carrying towel and shoes. Zhixiang took a liking to his quick wit.

sentences.zh: 時昶方就學，即命昭遠給事左右，而見親狎。

translations.literal: At that time Chang was just beginning his studies; he immediately ordered Zhaoyuan to attend at his side, and he was treated with intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: Chang was then still at his studies, and Zhixiang put Zhaoyuan in his service, where he grew intimate with the prince.

sentences.zh: 昶立，以為卷簾使。

translations.literal: When Chang took the throne he made him Curtain-Raising Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang took the throne he made him Curtain-Raising Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 樞密使王處回致仕，昶以樞密使權重難制，乃以昭遠為通奏使知樞密使事，然事無大小，一以委之，府庫金帛恣其所取不問。

translations.literal: When Chief Palace Secretary Wang Chuhui retired, Chang thought the office of Chief Palace Secretary was weighty and hard to control; he therefore made Zhaoyuan Memorial Transmission Commissioner acting Chief Palace Secretary. Yet matters great and small were all entrusted to him, and he took gold and silk from the treasury as he pleased without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Chuhui retired, Chang found the Chief Palace Secretary's office too powerful to control and made Zhaoyuan Memorial Transmission Commissioner acting in that role. Every matter, large or small, was left to him, and he helped himself to treasury gold and silk without question.

sentences.zh: 昶母李太后常為昶言昭遠不可用，昶不聽。

translations.literal: Chang's mother Empress Dowager Li often told Chang that Zhaoyuan could not be used, but Chang would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Li often told Chang that Zhaoyuan was unfit for office, but he would not listen.

sentences.zh: 昭遠好讀兵書，以方略自許。

translations.literal: Zhaoyuan loved reading military books and prided himself on strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoyuan loved military texts and fancied himself a strategist.

sentences.zh: 兵始發成都，昶遣李昊等餞之，昭遠手執鐵如意，指揮軍事，自比諸葛亮，酒酣，謂昊曰：「吾之是行，何止克敵，當領此二三萬雕面惡少兒，取中原如反掌爾！

translations.literal: As the army first set out from Chengdu, Chang sent Li Hao and others to see them off. Zhaoyuan held an iron ruyi scepter in his hand, directing military affairs and comparing himself to Zhuge Liang. When the wine had gone deep he said to Hao: "On this expedition of mine, how could it stop at defeating the enemy? I ought to lead these twenty or thirty thousand fierce-faced ruffians and take the central plains as easily as turning my palm!
translations.idiomatic: As the army left Chengdu, Chang sent Li Hao and others to see them off. Zhaoyuan gripped an iron ruyi scepter, directed the troops, and compared himself to Zhuge Liang. Deep in wine he told Hao: "This campaign will be more than defeating the enemy—I mean to lead these twenty or thirty thousand fierce young brutes and take the central plains as easily as turning my hand!

sentences.zh: 」昶又遣子玄喆率精兵數萬守劍門。

translations.literal: " Chang also sent his son Xuanzhe to lead several tens of thousands of elite troops to guard Sword Gate.
translations.idiomatic: " Chang also sent his son Xuanzhe with tens of thousands of elite troops to hold Sword Gate.

sentences.zh: 玄喆輦其愛姬，攜樂器、伶人數十以從，蜀人見者皆竊笑。

translations.literal: Xuanzhe had his beloved concubines carried in palanquins and brought several tens of musicians and actors with him; those who saw it in Shu all secretly laughed.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzhe brought his favorite concubines in palanquins and dozens of musicians and actors with him, and the people of Shu who saw it snickered behind their hands.

sentences.zh: 全斌至三泉，遇昭遠，擊敗之。

translations.literal: Quanbin reached Three Springs, encountered Zhaoyuan, and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Quanbin reached Three Springs, met Zhaoyuan, and routed him.

sentences.zh: 昭遠焚吉柏江浮橋，退守劍門。

translations.literal: Zhaoyuan burned the floating bridge on the Lucky Cypress River and withdrew to defend Sword Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoyuan burned the floating bridge on the Lucky Cypress River and fell back to Sword Gate.

sentences.zh: 軍頭向韜得蜀降卒言：「來蘇小路，出劍門南清強店，與大路合。

translations.literal: Army head Xiang Tao obtained a Shu surrendered soldier who said: "The Laisu bypath emerges south of Sword Gate at Qingqiang post station and joins the main road.
translations.idiomatic: Army head Xiang Tao learned from a surrendered Shu soldier: "The Laisu bypath runs south of Sword Gate from Qingqiang post station and joins the main road.

sentences.zh: 」全斌遣偏將史延德分兵出來蘇，北擊劍門，與全斌夾攻之，昭遠、彥韜敗走，皆見擒。

translations.literal: " Quanbin sent flank general Shi Yande with divided troops out by Laisu, striking Sword Gate from the north, while Quanbin attacked from both sides. Zhaoyuan and Yantao were defeated and fled; both were captured.
translations.idiomatic: " Quanbin sent flank general Shi Yande along the Laisu path to strike Sword Gate from the north while he attacked from the south. Zhaoyuan and Yantao were routed, fled, and were both captured.

sentences.zh: 玄喆聞昭遠等敗，亦逃歸。

translations.literal: Xuanzhe heard Zhaoyuan and the others were defeated and also fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of Zhaoyuan's defeat, Xuanzhe fled home as well.

sentences.zh: 劉光乂攻夔州，守將高彥儔戰敗，閉牙城拒守，判官羅濟勸其走，彥儔曰：「吾昔不能守秦川，今又奔北，雖人主不殺我，我何面目見蜀人乎！

translations.literal: Liu Guangyi attacked Kui Prefecture. Garrison commander Gao Yanchou was defeated in battle, closed the headquarters city and refused to yield. Administrative aide Luo Ji urged him to flee. Yanchou said: "I could not hold Qinchuan before; now if I flee north again, even if my lord does not kill me, what face have I to meet the people of Shu!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Guangyi attacked Kui Prefecture. Garrison commander Gao Yanchou was beaten, shut himself in the headquarters city, and refused to yield. Administrative aide Luo Ji urged flight. Yanchou said: "I failed to hold Qinchuan before; if I flee north again, even if the emperor spares me, what face have I to show the people of Shu!

sentences.zh: 」又勸其降，彥儔不許，乃自焚死。

translations.literal: " He again urged him to surrender; Yanchou would not agree and burned himself to death.
translations.idiomatic: " When Ji urged surrender, Yanchou refused and burned himself to death.

sentences.zh: 而蜀兵所在奔潰，將帥多被擒獲。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Shu troops everywhere broke and fled; generals and commanders were mostly captured.
translations.idiomatic: Shu troops everywhere broke and fled, and most commanders were captured.

sentences.zh: 昶問計於左右，老將石頵以謂東兵遠來，勢不能久，宜聚兵堅守以敝之。

translations.literal: Chang asked those at his side for a plan. The old general Shi Yun said that eastern troops had come from afar and by their momentum could not last long; they should gather troops and hold firm to wear them down.
translations.idiomatic: Chang asked his advisers for counsel. The veteran Shi Yun said the eastern army had come from far away and could not sustain a long campaign; they should mass their forces and hold out to wear the enemy down.

sentences.zh: 昶嘆曰：「吾與先君以溫衣美食養士四十年，一旦臨敵，不能為吾東向放一箭，雖欲堅壁，誰與吾守者邪！

translations.literal: Chang sighed and said: "My late father and I fed and clothed soldiers warmly for forty years; yet once we face the enemy they cannot shoot a single arrow eastward for me. Even if I wished to hold firm behind walls, who would hold them with me!
translations.idiomatic: Chang sighed: "My father and I clothed and fed these men generously for forty years, yet when the enemy comes not one will shoot an arrow eastward for me. Even if I wanted to hold behind walls, who would stand with me!

sentences.zh: 」乃命李昊草表以降，時乾德三年正月也。

translations.literal: " He then ordered Li Hao to draft a memorial of surrender; it was the first month of the third year of Qiande.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered Li Hao to draft the surrender memorial. It was the first month of the third year of Qiande.

sentences.zh: 自興師至昶降，凡六十六日。

translations.literal: From the raising of troops to Chang's surrender, altogether sixty-six days.
translations.idiomatic: From the opening of the campaign to Chang's surrender, sixty-six days had passed.

sentences.zh: 初，昊事王衍為翰林學士，衍之亡也，昊為草降表，至是又草焉，蜀人夜表其門曰「世修降表李家」，當時傳以為笑。

translations.literal: Earlier Hao had served Wang Yan as Hanlin Academician; when Yan perished Hao drafted the surrender memorial, and now drafted it again. The people of Shu posted on his gate by night the words "The Li family, hereditary drafters of surrender memorials," and at the time it was passed around as a joke.
translations.idiomatic: Hao had earlier served Wang Yan as Hanlin Academician and drafted Yan's surrender; now he drafted Chang's as well. The people of Shu posted on his gate by night: "The Li family—hereditary drafters of surrender memorials," and the line became a byword for ridicule.

sentences.zh: 昶至京師，拜檢校太師兼中書令，封秦國公，七日而卒，追封楚王。

translations.literal: Chang reached the capital, was invested as Acting Grand Preceptor and Director of the Secretariat, and enfeoffed as Duke of Qin; after seven days he died and was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Chang reached the capital, was made Acting Grand Preceptor and Director of the Secretariat, and enfeoffed Duke of Qin. He died seven days later and was posthumously enfeoffed Duke of Chu.

sentences.zh: 其母李氏，為人明辯，甚見優禮，詔書呼為「國母」，嘗召見勞之曰：「母善自愛，無戚戚思蜀，他日當送母歸。

translations.literal: His mother Lady Li was clear and sharp in speech and was greatly shown preferential courtesy; edicts addressed her as "State Mother." She was once summoned and comforted with the words: "Mother, take good care of yourself; do not sorrowfully long for Shu. Another day I shall send Mother home.
translations.idiomatic: His mother Lady Li was sharp-witted and treated with exceptional honor; edicts addressed her as State Mother. The emperor once summoned and comforted her: "Take good care of yourself, Mother; do not pine for Shu. One day I shall send you home.

sentences.zh: 」李氏曰：「妾家本太原，倘得歸老故鄉，不勝大願。

translations.literal: " Lady Li said: "My family is originally from Taiyuan; if I could return to grow old in my native place, I could not express my great wish more fully.
translations.idiomatic: " Lady Li said: "My family is from Taiyuan. To end my days in my native place would be my dearest wish.

sentences.zh: 」是時劉鈞尚在。

translations.literal: " At that time Liu Jun was still alive.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Jun of Northern Han was still alive at the time.

sentences.zh: 太祖大喜曰：「俟平劉鈞，當如母願。

translations.literal: The founding emperor was greatly pleased and said: "When Liu Jun is pacified, I shall fulfill Mother's wish.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor was delighted and said: "When Liu Jun is pacified, I shall grant your wish.

sentences.zh: 」昶之卒也，李氏不哭，以酒酹地祝曰：「汝不能死社稷，茍生以取羞。

translations.literal: " When Chang died, Lady Li did not weep. She poured wine on the ground in libation and prayed: "You could not die for the altars of soil and grain but lived in shame.
translations.idiomatic: " When Chang died, Lady Li did not weep. She poured a libation on the ground and prayed: "You could not die for your state but lived on in shame.

sentences.zh: 吾所以忍死者，以汝在也。

translations.literal: The reason I have endured living until now is that you were still alive.
translations.idiomatic: I have endured living only because you were still alive.

sentences.zh: 吾今何用生為！

translations.literal: What use have I in living now!
translations.idiomatic: What reason have I to go on living!

sentences.zh: 」因不食而卒。

translations.literal: " She then stopped eating and died.
translations.idiomatic: She thereupon stopped eating and died.

sentences.zh: 其餘事具國史。

translations.literal: The remaining matters are fully set forth in the national histories.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining events are recorded in full in the national histories.

translations.literal: An opening editorial bracket marking the start of an explanatory note.
translations.idiomatic: [Editorial note:

sentences.zh: （知祥興滅年數甚明，諸書皆同，蓋自同光三年乙酉入蜀，至皇朝乾德三年乙丑國滅，凡四十一年。

translations.literal: (The years of Zhixiang's rise and fall are very clear; all books are the same. Roughly from entering Shu in the third year of Tongguang, yiyou, until the state's destruction in the third year of Qiande of the present dynasty, yichou—in all forty-one years.
translations.idiomatic: (The span of Zhixiang's rise and fall is perfectly clear, and all books agree: from his entry into Shu in the third year of Tongguang (yiyou) until the state's destruction in the third year of Qiande of the present dynasty (yichou) is forty-one years in all.

sentences.zh: 惟《舊五代史》，雲同光三年丙戌至乾德三年乙丑，四十年者，繆也。）〉

translations.literal: Only the 《Old History of the Five Dynasties》 says from the third year of Tongguang, bingxu, to the third year of Qiande, yichou—forty years—is in error.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Only the 《Old History of the Five Dynasties》, which gives the third year of Tongguang (bingxu) to the third year of Qiande (yichou) as forty years, is mistaken.)]
